correctness.rationale: The exact product q_k(m)=∏_{j<k}d_j follows from the Catalan/Gödel generating-function recurrence and square-root coefficient extraction at r=1/(4m). The squared critical orbit X_j satisfies X_{j+1}=X_j+h/2-h²/(16X_j)+O(h³), uniformly 1/4≤X_j≤3/4. Its first correction is R(s)=-(log(1+2s))/8, with uniform O(h²) remainder by summing O(h³) step defects. The exact factors yield log d_j =h f_0(s_j)+h² f_1(s_j)+O(h³); uniform Euler summation to k≤m-1 and explicit integration give E(t). Endpoint k=m-1 shifts t by h and yields (8+log3)/12. A stdlib Python checker replays all product terms for m up to 2000, compares every cut with the expansion, and separately checks Catalan row-count DP for m=2..6,n≤8; VERIFY_OK. Finite tests supplement but do not replace the uniform proof.

value.rationale: The motivating recent work establishes a macroscopic limiting law but provides only coarse finite-chain convergence and numeric tables. The new nonconstant E(t) is an exact finite-resolution bias law across every possible truth-value threshold with one uniform O(m^-2) error, and yields the explicit top-atom rate (8+log3)/(12m). This is needed to approximate finite-valued semantics at controlled accuracy: at m=100, the top mass 0.581721832133 is improved from 0.577350269190 at leading order to 0.581727841068. The parameter range includes endpoints and moving cuts, not an arbitrary small numerical slice; the proof requires nontrivial second-order recurrence and endpoint accounting.
